title: assistant-tdd Skill Behavior Eval Fixtures
description: Provider-neutral offline eval cases for the assistant-tdd skill's Red-Green-Refactor enforcement.

activation_cases.user_request: Use TDD to fix this bug.
Write a failing regression test first.
Apply the known fix after the regression test already passes.

recommended_use: Run each case with the assistant-tdd skill instructions loaded.
Compare the local response against RED, GREEN, REFACTOR gate behavior and required RED evidence.
Use deterministic substring checks as offline proxies for contract adherence, not semantic grading.

cases.title: Bugfix starts with RED evidence
cases.purpose: Checks that active TDD begins with one meaningful failing assertion, which may extend an existing test, and records right-reason RED before production changes.
cases.prompt: Use TDD to fix the bug where the skill eval runner accepts duplicate case ids.
setup_context: The assistant-tdd skill instructions are active.
No failing regression test has been written yet.
expected_behavior: Activates Red-Green-Refactor and records TDD as active.
Starts with RED by adding or extending one meaningful behavior assertion.
Runs the test and verifies that it fails for the right reason.
Captures RED evidence including test file, test name, command run, failure summary, and why it proves the missing behavior.
Blocks production implementation until the failing test evidence exists.
Does not batch multiple unrelated behaviors into the first RED step.
pass_criteria: The response names RED as the first phase.
The response requires one meaningful failing assertion before production code.
The response requires the failure to be for the right reason.
The response lists the RED evidence needed before GREEN.
The response refuses to write production code before RED evidence.
fail_signals: Writes several behavior tests in one RED cycle.
Treats a syntax error or missing import as a valid RED failure.
Promises to add tests after fixing the bug.

forbidden_substrings: I will fix the code first

cases.title: GREEN and REFACTOR run selected regressions
cases.purpose: Checks that GREEN and REFACTOR run the selected target, relevant regressions, and binding suites without requiring unselected full-suite tests.
cases.prompt: The RED test is failing for the expected missing duplicate-id validation. Continue the TDD cycle.
setup_context: The assistant-tdd skill instructions are active.
A valid RED test has already failed for the intended missing behavior.
Production implementation has not yet started.
expected_behavior: Moves to GREEN only because RED evidence is present.
Implements the simplest production change needed to pass the failing test.
Runs the previously failing test and confirms it now passes.
Runs selected regression checks and binding project suites.
Uses REFACTOR only for behavior-neutral cleanup.
Runs selected checks and binding regressions after REFACTOR and starts the next behavior with a new RED cycle.
pass_criteria: The response gates GREEN on prior RED evidence.
The response limits implementation to the simplest passing code.
The response runs targeted checks and selected regressions in GREEN.
The response runs selected checks and binding regressions after REFACTOR.
fail_signals: Skips a selected regression or binding suite.
Starts the next behavior without a new RED cycle.

cases.title: TDD covers carried architecture obligations
cases.purpose: Checks that TDD turns a carried Architecture Decision Pack into focused semantic and quality verification rather than generic wrapper tests or unsupported quality claims.
cases.prompt: Use TDD for an import API that replaces string record IDs with ImportRecordId and claims its batch path uses less memory.
setup_context: The assistant-tdd skill instructions are active.

architecture_test_obligations includes stable obligation_id values for semantic_type_validation, primitive_boundary_conversion, public_contract_compatibility, quality_scenario, control_or_early_exit, and ownership_or_disposal obligations from a fresh Pack.
The memory claim has a representative workload but no agreed budget or failure condition yet.
expected_behavior: Starts with focused RED tests for semantic validation/conversion and compatibility behavior.
Does not treat a type wrapper that compiles as sufficient coverage.
Adds focused behavior evidence for early exit and ownership/disposal when those Pack obligations apply.
Marks the memory claim as blocked or explicit_unknown until workload, budget or explicit unknown, measurement method, and failure condition are defined.
Returns architecture_obligation_coverage with Pack reference and evidence/outcome, binding each input obligation exactly once by obligation_id.
pass_criteria: The response mentions architecture_test_obligations and architecture_obligation_coverage.
The response names semantic type, conversion or validation, compatibility, early exit, ownership or disposal, workload, budget, measurement, and failure condition.
fail_signals: Claims the memory improvement from an unmeasured architecture choice.
Uses compilation of a wrapper as the only test.
Skips RED because the Pack already chose the design.

forbidden_substrings: wrapper compiles so it is covered

cases.title: Unknown-cause bugfix waits for debugging evidence
cases.purpose: Checks that assistant-tdd refuses to start RED for unknown-cause bugs until assistant-debugging evidence can define a meaningful regression test.
cases.prompt: Use TDD to fix the intermittent checkout total bug, but I do not have a reproduction yet.
setup_context: The assistant-tdd skill instructions are active.
The bug is unknown-cause and lacks a reproduction path.
expected_behavior: Does not start a TDD cycle immediately.
Routes to assistant-debugging or equivalent fallback first.
Requires reproduction/root-cause evidence before RED.
Records debugging evidence needed for the regression test.
pass_criteria: The response says RED is blocked until meaningful debugging evidence exists.
The response requires reproduction/root-cause evidence and original failure path.
fail_signals: Writes a test before the failure mechanism is known.
Says any generic failing test is enough.
